Systemgrenze und architektonische Rolle im Zusammenspiel mit Execution Management

Das funktionale Cluster State Management (SM) definiert und steuert den übergeordneten Betriebs- und Funktionszustand der AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform (SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4 „State Management“). Während das SM die betriebliche Arbitrierung übernimmt und Zielzustände vorgibt, führt das Execution Management (EM) die konkreten Zustandswechsel durch, indem es zugehörige Prozesse startet oder terminiert (EXP SWArchitecture §9.2.1.1 „Defined interfaces“). Das SM interagiert hierfür über die Schnittstelle ara::exec::StateClient ([SWS_SM_00400], EXP SWArchitecture §9.2.1.1.2 „Interfaces for State Management“). Die Systemzustände gliedern sich in den Lebenszyklus der gesamten Machine (den sogenannten Machine State innerhalb der MachineFG) sowie applikative Funktionsgruppenzustände (Function Group States) (SWS StateManagement §7.1.1 „Machine State“).

Beim Plattformstart wird das Execution Management als primärer Prozess durch das Betriebssystem initiiert und startet selbsttätig den Übergang in den Zustand Startup der MachineFG ([SWS_EM_01023], EXP SWArchitecture §11.1 „Architecture“). Es ist zwingend vorgeschrieben, dass das State Management im Startup-Zustand konfiguriert ist, da die Machine andernfalls in keinem weiteren Zustand manövrierfähig wäre (SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4.2.1 „Startup“). Sobald der Startup-Zustand erreicht ist, meldet das EM den Abschluss an das SM ([SWS_EM_02241]), woraufhin das SM die volle Verantwortung für die Initiierung weiterer Zustandswechsel übernimmt (SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4.2 „Startup transition“). Ebenso muss das SM in den Zuständen Shutdown und Restart lauffähig bleiben, um Fehlerbehandlungen und kontrollierte Abschaltungen abzuwickeln (SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4.2.1 „Startup“, SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4.2.2 „Shutdown“).

Kontextdiagramm: Architektonische Einbettung von State Management zwischen Steuerungsanwendung, Execution Management, Plattformüberwachung und Plattformdiensten. Quellen: SWS StateManagement §5 „Interfaces provided by State Management“, EXP SWArchitecture §9.2.1.1.2 „Interfaces for State Management“

Zustandsmaschinen-Architektur: Controller- und Agent-Hierarchie

Die interne Architektur des State Management unterstützt neben einer frei implementierbaren Arbitrierungslogik den standardisierten StateMachine-Ansatz (SWS StateManagement §7.1.3 „Arbitration logic“). Dieser trennt die projektspezifische Anwendungslogik, die in einer externen SMControlApplication liegt, von der Plattformausführung (SWS StateManagement §7.7.2 „Controlling application for StateMachine States“). Innerhalb dieses Ansatzes existiert eine zweistufige Hierarchie aus genau einer Controller-Zustandsmaschine und mehreren untergeordneten Agent-Zustandsmaschinen (SWS StateManagement §7.7.4 „StateMachine Types“, SWS StateManagement §7.7.8 „Controlling multiple StateMachine Instances“).

Der Controller wird beim Hochfahren des State-Management-Prozesses gestartet ([SWS_SM_00648]) und ist exklusiv für den Lebenszyklus der gesamten Machine verantwortlich: Alle Aktionslisten des Controllers müssen daher zwingend den Funktionsgruppenzustand für MachineFG referenzieren ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00017]). Zudem besitzt ausschließlich der Controller die Berechtigung, untergeordnete Agent-Instanzen über die Aktionen StartStateMachine und StopStateMachine zu starten oder zu beenden ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00019]). Tiefer verschachtelte Hierarchien sind unzulässig (SWS StateManagement §7.7.8 „Controlling multiple StateMachine Instances“). Jede Aktionsliste des Controllers muss dabei die vollständige Menge der kontrollierten Agenten referenzieren ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00016]).

Die Agent-Zustandsmaschinen steuern applikative Funktionsgruppen. Um funktionale Kollisionen zu verhindern, darf jede Funktionsgruppe im Gesamtsystem durch genau eine Zustandsmaschine referenziert werden ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00013]). Darüber hinaus dürfen Agenten nur solche Funktionsgruppen verwalten, die demselben Software Cluster (claimedFunctionGroups) zugeordnet sind ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00018]). Jeder konfigurierte Agent muss über einen definierten Off-Zustand verfügen ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00024]), in dem ausschließlich die Zuweisungen Function Group::Off, NmNetworkHandle::NoCom, SYNC und Sleep zulässig sind ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00011]). Wird ein Agent gestoppt, so wird er geordnet in seinen Off-Zustand überführt ([SWS_SM_00651]), bevor er vollständig aufhört zu existieren ([SWS_SM_00614]).

Strukturdiagramm: Hierarchische Beziehung zwischen Controller-StateMachine und untergeordneten Agent-StateMachines sowie deren Function-Group-Zuordnung. Quellen: [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00017], [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00018], SWS StateManagement §7.7.2 „Function Group controlled by single StateMachine“

Zustandswechsel werden von der SMControlApplication über die servicebasierte Methode RequestTransition der Schnittstelle StateMachineService beauftragt ([SWS_SM_00600], [SWS_SM_91107]). Das SM prüft die Anfrage anhand der projektierten TransitionRequestTable (SWS StateManagement §7.7.3 „TransitionRequestTable“). Ist der Übergang aus dem aktuellen Zustand nicht modelliert, wird die Anfrage mit kTransitionNotAllowed abgewiesen ([SWS_SM_00603]); bei unbekanntem Übergangswert erfolgt die Rückweisung mit kInvalidValue ([SWS_SM_00604]). Befindet sich das Modul bereits in einer Fehlerbehebung, wird der Aufruf mit kRecoveryTransitionOngoing blockiert ([SWS_SM_00605]). Während eines laufenden Wechsels nimmt das Notifikationsfeld CurrentState den Wert "inTransition" an ([SWS_SM_00616], [SWS_SM_91109]) und wird erst nach erfolgreicher Vollendung aller Aktionen auf den Zielzustandsnamen gesetzt ([SWS_SM_00617]).

Sequenzdiagramm: Ablauf eines Zustandswechsels auf Anforderung der Steuerungsanwendung mit Validierung und EM-Aktionslisten. Quellen: [SWS_SM_91107], [SWS_SM_00608], EXP SWArchitecture §11.1.2 „Scenario: Change System State“

Ablaufsteuerung über Aktionslisten, Synchronisation und Netzwerkbindung

Jeder Zustand einer StateMachine ist mit einer geordneten ActionList verknüpft, die einzelne Aktionsschritte (ActionListItem) bündelt (SWS StateManagement §7.7.7 „ActionListItems“). Zu den standardisierten Elementtypen gehören Function Group State zur Auslösung von Prozesswechseln im EM ([SWS_SM_00608]), SetNetworkHandle für Netzwerkanforderungen ([SWS_SM_00625]), Sleep für zeitliche Verzögerungen ([SWS_SM_00624]), SYNC zur Synchronisation sowie Kommandos für Suspend-to-RAM (SWS StateManagement §7.7.7 „ActionListItems“). Um eine konsistente Konfiguration zu gewährleisten, muss jede Aktionsliste einer Zustandsmaschine stets dieselbe Menge an Funktionsgruppen ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00015]) und Netzwerk-Handles ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00032]) abbilden.

Die Abarbeitung der Elemente erfolgt standardmäßig parallel: Nachfolgende Aktionsschritte werden unmittelbar angestoßen, es sei denn, ein explizites SYNC-Element erzwingt das Abwarten aller bisherigen Rückmeldungen ([SWS_SM_00611]). Am Ende jeder ActionList existiert zudem ein implizites SYNC, sodass die Aktionsliste erst als abgeschlossen gilt, wenn alle Einzelschritte ausgeführt und sämtliche asynchronen Antworten eingetroffen sind ([SWS_SM_00667]). Die Gesamtlaufzeit einer Aktionsliste wird zeitlich überwacht ([SWS_SM_00669]); wird kein individueller Timeout konfiguriert, greift der globale Parameter maxActionListDuration der Modulinstanz ([SWS_SM_00668]).

Über das Network Management (NM) kann das State Management Kommunikationskanäle aktivieren (FullCom) oder deaktivieren (NoCom) ([SWS_SM_00625], [SWS_SM_00626]). Analog zur Funktionsgruppenbindung darf auch jedes NmNetworkHandle nur von genau einer Zustandsmaschine gesteuert werden ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00025]). Wechselt der Status eines Netzwerk-Handles asynchron von extern, reagiert die Zustandsmaschine unverzüglich: Die laufende Aktionsliste wird abgebrochen und direkt in den für dieses Ereignis projektierten Folgezustand gewechselt ([SWS_SM_00620], [SWS_SM_00621]).

Aktivitätsdiagramm: Parallele Ausführung von Aktionslistenelementen und Synchronisationsbarrieren via SYNC. Quellen: [SWS_SM_00611], [SWS_SM_00667], SWS StateManagement §7.7.7 „processing ActionListItem“

Suspend-to-RAM-Koordination über S2R-Hub und Satelliten

Zur Optimierung von Start- und Abschaltzeiten unterstützt das State Management den Modus Suspend-to-RAM (S2R) (SWS StateManagement §7.5 „Interaction with Suspend-to-RAM Functionality“). Applikationen deklarieren im Manifest ihre Eignung über das Attribut suspendToRamAwareness (SWS StateManagement §7.8.4 „Suspend-to-RAM awareness“): Prozesse mit suspendToRamNotSupported müssen vor dem Suspend durch das SM geordnet über Funktionsgruppenwechsel beendet werden (SWS StateManagement §7.8.4.2 „Suspend-to-RAM not supported“). Prozesse mit dem Status suspendToRamAware werden hingegen aktiv synchronisiert (SWS StateManagement §7.8.4.3 „Suspend-to-RAM aware“).

Hierzu stellt das State Management das Komponentenpaar S2RHub ([SWS_SM_81103]) und S2RSatellite ([SWS_SM_81003]) bereit (SWS StateManagement §7.5.1 „S2R Hub“). Satelliten bieten ihre Bereitschaft über Offer() an ([SWS_SM_81012], [SWS_SM_00710]). Um unbefugte Manipulationen zu verhindern, prüft der Hub bei Instanziierung und Registrierung die IAM-Berechtigungen; bei Verstößen wird das Sicherheitsereignis SEV_ACCESS_CONTROL_SM_IAM_ACCESS_DENIED ausgelöst ([SWS_SM_00706], [SWS_SM_00714], [SWS_SM_00715], [SWS_SM_70001]). Wird der StateMachine-Ansatz verwendet, kapselt der Controller die Hub-Funktionalität intern vollständig; eine externe Nutzung der Hub-C++-API ist in diesem Fall strikt untersagt ([SWS_SM_00684]).

Beim Einleiten des Ruhezustands ruft der Hub über RequestToEnterSuspendMode die Callbacks EnterSuspendMode() aller aktiven Satelliten asynchron auf ([SWS_SM_81110], [SWS_SM_81010], [SWS_SM_00701]). Nach Bestätigung aller Satelliten triggert das SM über EnterSuspendToRamOs() den Betriebssystemübergang ([SWS_SM_81112], [SWS_SM_00692]) unter Nutzung der OS-Schnittstelle SetPowerState mit dem Enum-Wert kPmSuspendToRam ([SWS_SM_71001], [SWS_SM_71002]). Beim Aufwachen koordinieren RequestToLeaveSuspendMode und LeaveSuspendMode() die Wiederinbetriebnahme ([SWS_SM_81111], [SWS_SM_81011], [SWS_SM_00703]). Das SM kann über den WakeUpHandler im OS-Wrapper auch autonom auf Aufweckereignisse reagieren ([SWS_SM_71003], [SWS_SM_71004], SWS StateManagement §7.7.15.1 „Autonomous wake-up from suspend state“). Hierfür muss der Controller einen dezidierten Zustand LeaveSuspend besitzen ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00036]), welcher das Aktionslistenelement LeaveSuspendToRam enthält ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00037]).

Sequenzdiagramm: Koordinierter Ablauf des Suspend-to-RAM-Eintritts über S2RHub, Satelliten und Betriebssystemaufruf. Quellen: [SWS_SM_81110], [SWS_SM_81010], [SWS_SM_81112], SWS StateManagement §7.5 „Interaction between S2RSatellite and S2RHub“

Interaktion mit Update and Configuration Management während Fahrzeug-Updates

Während Software-Aktualisierungen arbeitet das State Management eng mit dem Update and Configuration Management (UCM) zusammen (SWS StateManagement §7.7.14 „StateMachine support for Update and Configuration Management“). Hierzu stellt das SM die Service-Schnittstelle UpdateRequest bereit ([SWS_SM_91016], [SWS_SM_91017]). Im Kontext einer Machine darf exakt ein Port für diese Schnittstelle existieren ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020]), der zwingend vom Prozess des Controller instanziiert werden muss ([SWS_SM_00629]). Ob eine Aktualisierung zulässig ist, bestimmt die SMControlApplication über das Service-Feld UpdateAllowed ([SWS_SM_91108], SWS StateManagement §7.4 „Update session“). Ist dieses auf kUpdateNotAllowed gesetzt, weist das SM den Aufruf RequestUpdateSession mit kOperationRejected ab ([SWS_SM_00630], [SWS_SM_91102]).

Wird eine Update-Sitzung akzeptiert, gilt diese als aktiv ([SWS_SM_00210]). Das SM persistiert diesen Zustand resilient, sodass er auch nach einem Reboot abrufbar bleibt ([SWS_SM_00204]). Parallele Update-Sitzungen sind unzulässig ([SWS_SM_00209]). Die Aktualisierung gliedert sich in methodische Schritte: Über PrepareUpdate übergibt das UCM eine Liste betroffener Funktionsgruppen ([SWS_SM_91103]). Das SM markiert die zugehörigen Agent-Zustandsmaschinen als "ImpactedByUpdate" ([SWS_SM_00654]), wodurch transitiv auch der Controller als "ImpactedByUpdate" gekennzeichnet wird ([SWS_SM_00655]). Sämtliche betroffenen Agenten werden daraufhin gestoppt ([SWS_SM_00634]), und normale Zustandswechselanfragen via RequestTransition werden mit kUpdateInProgress blockiert ([SWS_SM_00649]).

Für die anschließende Prüfung muss jede Zustandsmaschine über einen modellierten Zustand VerifyUpdate verfügen ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00022]), der bei Aufruf von VerifyUpdate eingenommen wird ([SWS_SM_00638], [SWS_SM_91104]). Für Rollback-Szenarien existiert analog der Pflichtzustand PrepareRollback ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00023], [SWS_SM_00642], [SWS_SM_91105]). Verlangt das UCM über ResetMachine einen Neustart ([SWS_SM_91100]), wechselt der Controller in den Zustand Restart ([SWS_SM_00658]). Nach dem anschließenden Maschinenstart fährt das SM aufgrund der aktiven Update-Sitzung in den Zustand ContinueUpdate anstelle des regulären Initial-Zustands hoch ([SWS_SM_00657]) und meldet den Status über das Feld ResetMachineNotifier an das UCM ([SWS_SM_00662], [SWS_SM_91106]). Beendet wird die Sitzung über StopUpdateSession, woraufhin der Controller in den Zustand AfterUpdate übergeht ([SWS_SM_00205], [SWS_SM_00646], [SWS_SM_91101]).

Verhalten im Fehlerfall und Überwachungsreaktionen

Das Platform Health Management (PHM) überwacht Applikationen und meldet festgestellte Überwachungsfehler über den Callback RecoveryHandler() an das State Management (EXP SWArchitecture §11.1.2.2.1 „Scenario: Recover by System State Change“, EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.2 „Scenario: Report Supervision Failure“). Um auf Fehler reagieren zu können, muss sich das SM vorab über Offer() beim PHM registrieren (EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.2 „Scenario: Report Supervision Failure“). Reagiert das SM nicht innerhalb des im Manifest konfigurierten Timeouts auf den RecoveryHandler(), eskaliert das PHM über FireWatchdogReaction() zu einem harten Maschinen-Reset (EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.2 „Scenario: Report Supervision Failure“). Ebenso führt ein kritischer Fehler im SM-Prozess selbst direkt zur Watchdog-Auslösung (EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.3.1 „Scenario: Recover from Critical Supervision Failure in State Management“).

Im StateMachine-Ansatz wird die Fehlerbehebung über die ErrorRecoveryTable deklariert (SWS StateManagement §7.7.13 „ErrorRecoveryTable“). Um lückenlose Fehlerabdeckung sicherzustellen, muss jede Fehlertabelle exakt einen Eintrag mit dem Fehlercode ANY aufweisen, der als Auffangregel für nicht explizit zugeordnete Fehler dient ([SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014]). Sobald eine Fehlerreaktion initiiert wird, setzt die Zustandsmaschine das interne Flag ErrorRecoveryOngoing, bricht die laufende Aktionsliste ab und startet unmittelbar die Aktionsliste des Wiederherstellungszustands ([SWS_SM_00601]). Das Flag bleibt aktiv und blockiert reguläre Übergänge, bis alle Aktionsschritte der Fehlerreaktion erfolgreich abgeschlossen sind ([SWS_SM_00602]). Treten währenddessen weitere Fehler auf, greift die verschachtelte Fehlerbehandlung (Nested Recovery) ([SWS_SM_00031], [SWS_SM_00666]). Meldet das SM dem PHM, dass es einen Fehler nicht beheben kann (Fehlercode kSMCanNotHandleRecovery), löst das PHM den Watchdog-Reset aus (EXP SWArchitecture §11.1.2.2.2 „Scenario: Recover by Watchdog Reset“).

Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklus und Verzweigung der Fehlerbehandlung mit ErrorRecoveryTable und Flag ErrorRecoveryOngoing. Quellen: [SWS_SM_00601], [SWS_SM_00602], [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014], SWS StateManagement §7.7.13 „ErrorRecoveryTable“

Fehler bei Schnittstellenaufrufen werden über die C++-Fehlerdomäne SmErrorDomain ([SWS_SM_81247], [SWS_SM_81251], [SWS_SM_91010]) mit dem Bezeichner "Sm" ([SWS_SM_81248]) abgebildet. Der Enumerator SmErrc definiert systemspezifische Fehlercodes wie kOfferFailed (Dienstangebot fehlgeschlagen) und kCommunicationFailed (Kommunikationsabbruch zu Satelliten) ([SWS_SM_81240], [SWS_SM_81244]). Im Ausnahmefall können diese Fehler über ThrowAsException als SmException geworfen werden, sofern C++-Exceptions in der Plattform aktiviert sind ([SWS_SM_81243], [SWS_SM_81250]).

Weiterführende Detailbelege

Die normative Basis des Moduls State Management stützt sich auf folgende zentrale Spezifikationsanker:

  • Prozess- und Zustandssteuerung: [SWS_SM_00400] verankert die Nutzung der StateClient-API gegenüber dem Execution Management; [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00017] und [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00019] definieren die Alleinstellung des Controller für MachineFG und die Agent-Steuerung (SWS StateManagement §7.7.4, SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4.5).
  • Aktionslisten und Synchronisation: [SWS_SM_00608], [SWS_SM_00611] und [SWS_SM_00667] regeln die parallele Ausführung von Aktionslistenelementen und die Synchronisationspunkte über SYNC (SWS StateManagement §7.7.7).
  • Fehlerbehandlung und Resilienz: [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014] fordert den lückenlosen ANY-Fallback in Fehlertabellen; [SWS_SM_00601] und [SWS_SM_00602] steuern das Sperrflag während aktiver Fehlerreaktionen (SWS StateManagement §7.7.13).
  • Fahrzeug-Update (UCM): [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020], [SWS_SM_00204], [SWS_SM_00210] und [SWS_SM_00657] sichern die exklusive Instanziierung des UpdateRequest-Ports, die Persistierung von Update-Sitzungen und den Start in ContinueUpdate nach einem Reboot (SWS StateManagement §7.4, SWS StateManagement §7.7.14).
  • Schnellstart (Suspend-to-RAM): [SWS_SM_00701], [SWS_SM_00714], [SWS_SM_81110] und [SWS_SM_81112] normieren die IAM-gesicherte Orchestrierung von Satelliten und die OS-Übergabe über den S2RHub (SWS StateManagement §7.5.1).

RICHTLINIEN (bindend):
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

LEITBILD (Umfang und Aufbau orientieren sich an den bewährten Adaptive-Modulleitfäden):
- 900–1600 Wörter in 5–8 thematischen Abschnitten mit <h4>-Überschriften, die das
  Modul erschließen (z. B. Rolle und Systemgrenze, zentrale Abläufe vom Start bis zur
  Nutzung, Daten- und Interaktionsformen, Betriebsregeln und Randbedingungen,
  Konfiguration/Instanzbezug, Verhalten im Fehlerfall). Die Überschriften sind
  modulspezifisch zu formulieren, nicht generisch.
- Ein Abschnitt „Verhalten im Fehlerfall“ und am Ende ein Abschnitt
  „Weiterführende Detailbelege“ (die wichtigsten Requirements/Dokumentstellen kurz
  eingeordnet).
- Jeder Absatz enthält mindestens einen Beleg (Requirement-ID oder Dokumentstelle).
- 4–10 Diagramme, wo sie Mehrwert bieten: Sequenzdiagramme für zentrale Abläufe,
  Zustandsdiagramme für Lebenszyklen, Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramme für die
  Einbettung, Aktivitätsdiagramme für Entscheidungen. Die Schaubilder der Spezifikation
  (Payload-Einträge mit "figure": true) sind Ausgangspunkt: übernimm ihre Aussage,
  wo sie den Text stützen, und verbessere ihre Lesbarkeit.
- Das Fragment beginnt mit <div class="ai module-guide"> und endet mit
  <p class="ai-note">…</p></div>.

AUSGABEFORMAT (verbindlich, nichts außerhalb dieser Blöcke):
<<<FRAGMENT
<div class="…"> … </div>
FRAGMENT>>>
Danach je Diagramm-Platzhalter genau ein Block:
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> seq
<JSON nach dem Sequenz-Schema>
DIAGRAM>>>
oder
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> dot
<Graphviz-digraph ohne Stilattribute (Farben/Schriften setzt der Generator)>
DIAGRAM>>>

Sequenz-Schema (JSON):
{"titel": str, "teilnehmer": [{"name": str}], "schritte": [
  {"art": "nachricht", "von": <idx>, "nach": <idx>, "text": [str], "pfeil": "voll"|"offen", "gestrichelt": bool},
  {"art": "selbst", "teilnehmer": <idx>, "text": [str]},
  {"art": "notiz", "ueber": [<idx>, <idx>], "text": [str]},
  {"art": "abschnitt", "text": str},
  {"art": "rahmen", "typ": "alt"|"opt"|"loop", "guard": str}, {"art": "trenner", "guard": str}, {"art": "rahmen-ende"}
]}
Antworten/Rückgaben: "pfeil": "offen", "gestrichelt": true. Zustands-, Kontext- und Aktivitätsdiagramme als dot.

   "text": "Architecture\nhandling low-level middleware. The AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform demands that the\nWatchdog\nis enabled prior to the startup of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform, for ex-\nample, the\nWatchdog\ncould already be enabled by the\nBootloader\nor the\nOperat-\ning System\n.\nExecution Management\nis started by the\nOperating System\nas the first process\nof the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform.\nExecution Management\nthen controls the\nstartup of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform by activating the standardized\nFunction\nGroup State\ncalled\nStartup\nof the\nMachine Function Group State\n. This trig-\ngers the start of additional processes that are configured to run in the\nStartup\nstate. It\nis mandatory that\nState Management\nis part of the\nStartup\nstate. Other processes\nof the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform, for example\nPlatform Health Management\nand application processes may also be part of the\nStartup\nstate (see Figure 11.1).\nPlatform Health Management\nis responsible to…"
  },

   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_S_P217_349",
   "page": 217,
   "text": "Architecture\nFigure 11.2 shows the default scenario for\nShutdown Adaptive Platform\nwith a\nsupervision of Adaptive Applications. It therefore includes the shutdown of\nPlatform\nHealth Management\nthat performs supervision.\nThe shutdown is triggered by\nState Management\nby requesting the standardized\nMachine Function Group State\ncalled\nShutdown\n. In general, it is assumed that\nthe only processes configured to run in the\nShutdown\nstate are\nExecution Man-\nagement\n,\nState Management\n, and an application that issues a shutdown request\ntowards the\nOperating System\n(\nshutdownApp\nin Figure 11.2). That application\nis usually specific for the\nOperating System\nand/or project and therefore not an\nAdaptive Application. The use of an external application that performs the shutdown\nkeeps\nExecution Management\nfree from project-specific functionality.\nExecution\nManagement\nwill perform an orderly shutdown of the other running application and\nplatform p…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 11,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_S_P218_350",
   "page": 218,
   "text": "Figure 11.3: Scenario: Change Function Group State\nFigure 11.3 shows the default scenario for\nChange Function Group State\n. The\nscenario is triggered by\nState Management\n.\nExecution Management\nwill termi-\nnate all processes that are not part of the requested target\nFunction Group State\nor that have a different\nStateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nJust before terminating a process (with a\nSIGTERM\nsignal),\nExecution Manage-\nment\nnotifies\nPlatform Health Management\nthat will stop all supervisions of the\nprocess. Consequently,\nState Management\nwill not receive any information about\nfailed supervisions during the shutdown of the process. The shutdown is monitored by\nExecution Management\nby means of\nStartupConfig\n.\ntimeout\nconfigured in the\nManifest\n.\nAfterwards,\nExecution Management\nstarts the processes of the target\nFunction\nGroup State\nin the order imposed by their\nStateDependentStartupConfig\n.\nWhen a processes reports its execution state a…"
  },
  {

   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_S_P219_352",
   "page": 219,
   "text": "Figure 11.4: Scenario: Change System State\nFigure 11.4 shows the default scenario for\nChange System State\n. An\nSMCon-\ntrolApplication\ncalls\nRequestTransition\nwith a parameter indicating the re-\nquested transition. Based on the requested transition,\nState Management\ndeter-\nmines a new desired system state, that is a set of desired\nFunction Group State\ns,\nand requests these\nFunction Group State\ns from\nExecution Management\nby\ncalling\nSetState()\n.\n11.1.2.2 Recover from Supervision Failure\n11.1.2.2.1 Scenario: Recover by System State Change"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 11,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_S_P220_353",
   "page": 220,
   "text": "Figure 11.5: Scenario: Recover by System State Change\nFigure 11.5 shows the default scenario for\nRecover from Supervision Failure\n.\nAfter a supervision failure has been detected by\nPlatform Health Management\n,\nPlatform Health Management\nnotifies\nState Management\nby invoking the call-\nback method\nRecoveryHandler()\n.\nState Management\nthen determines a new\ndesired state (which may be the same as the current state) and requests corresponding\nFunction Group State\ntransitions from\nExecution Management\n.\n11.1.2.2.2 Scenario: Recover by Watchdog Reset"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 11,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_S_P220_354",
   "page": 220,
   "text": "Figure 11.6: Scenario: Recover by Watchdog Reset\nFigure 11.6 shows an alternate scenario for\nRecover from Supervision Fail-\nure\n. After a supervision failure has been detected by\nPlatform Health Manage-\nment\n,\nPlatform Health Management\nnotifies\nState Management\nby invoking\nthe call-back method\nRecoveryHandler()\n. In this scenario,\nState Management\ncannot handle the failure and returns the error code\nkSMCanNotHandleRecovery"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 11,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_S_P234_355",
   "page": 234,
   "text": "Figure 11.23: Scenario: Report Supervision Failure\nFigure 11.23 illustrates the default scenario for\nReport Supervision Failure\n. As\na precondition,\nState Management\nneeds to call the method\nOffer()\nin order to\nregister for notifications.\nWhenever\nPlatform Health Management\ndetects a supervision failure it notifies\nState Management\nby invoking the callback method\nRecoveryHandler()\n. If the\ncall to\nState Management\ndoes not return within the timeout configured in the\nMan-\nifest\n,\nPlatform Health Management\nneeds to call the method\nFireWatchdo-\ngReaction()\nto perform a restart of the\nMachine\n.\nDuring its shutdown\nState Management\nneeds to call the method\nStopOffer()\nto\ndisable further invocations of\nRecoveryHandler()\n.\n11.5.1.3 Recover from Critical Supervision Failure\n11.5.1.3.1 Scenario: Recover from Critical Supervision Failure in Execution\nManagement"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 11,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture",
   "figure": true,

   "page": 235,
   "text": "Figure 11.25: Scenario: Recover from Critical Supervision Failure in State Management\nThe figure 11.25 shows a scenario for\nReport Supervision Failure\nthat han-\ndles recovery from a critical supervision failure in\nState Management\n. Such failures\nare considered as critical failures because\nState Management\nis required to recover\nfrom supervision failures. Thus, a supervision failure in\nState Management\nresults\nin\nPlatform Health Management\ncalling the method\nFireWatchdogReaction\n()\nto perform a restart of the\nMachine\n.\n11.5.1.4 Report Checkpoint\n11.5.1.4.1 Scenario: Report Checkpoint"

   "text": "Please note the API defines the execution context of the termination handler to be a\nbackground thread which is maintained by the\nara::exec::ExecutionClient\n. It\nis not executed in a signal handler context, therefore usage of POSIX and\nara\nAPIs is\nnot restricted (potential restrictions in the contract of\nara\nAPIs still apply).\nDuring the\nTerminating\nstate, the\nProcess\nis expected to save persistent data and\nfree all internally used resources. The\nProcess\nindicates completion of the\nTermi-\nnating\nstate by termination with exit status 0 (\nEXIT_SUCCESS\n).\nExecution Management\nas the parent\nProcess\ncan detect termination of the child\nProcess\nand take the appropriate platform-specific actions such as processing exe-\ncution dependencies that rely on the\nTerminated\nstate and thus ensure that there is\nno overlap between these\nProcesses\nwhen both are running.\n[SWS_EM_01314] Default value for terminationBehavior\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_EM…"

This is\nguaranteed by [SWS_EM_02542]. During the transition,\nExecution Manage-\nment\nrequests startup of\nProcesses\nthat exist in the\nStartup Machine State\n.\nAfter the necessary state transition conditions have been met (see Section 7.4.5 and\nSection 7.4.2.1),\nExecution Management\nreports\nMachine State Startup\ntran-\nsition confirmation to\nState Management\n([SWS_EM_02241]).    "text": "7.4 State Management\n7.4.1 Overview\nState Management\nfunctional cluster defines the operational state of an\nAUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n, while\nExecution Management\nperforms the transitions be-\ntween different states.\nThe\nExecution Manifest\nallows to define in which states the\nModelled Pro-\ncesses\nhave to run (see [3]). As mentioned before, a\nModelled Process\nis an\ninstance of an\nExecutable\n, which is part of an\nAdaptive Application\n.\nState\nManagement\nmechanisms grant full control over the set of applications to be executed\nand ensures that\nProcesses\nare only executed (and hence resources allocated) when\nactually needed.\nFour different states are relevant for\nExecution Management\n:\nExecution State\n– An Execution States characterizes the internal lifecycle of each\nstarted\nProcess\n, see Section 7.3.1\nProcess State\n–\nProcess States\nare managed by an\nExecution Management\ninternal state machine. For details see Section 7.3.2.\nMachine Sta…"

In that event\nExecution Management\ncan’t be sure what level of functionality is\navailable and if a failed state transition can be handled by\nState Management\n. It is\nworth to note that the\nState Management\nitself can be unavailable or its functionality\ncan be very limited at that point in time.\n[SWS_EM_02241] Machine State Startup Completion…"

   "text": "The specification expects that\nState Management\nwill be configured to run in ev-\nery\nMachine State\n(this includes\nStartup\n,\nShutdown\nand\nRestart\n) [SWS_SM_\nCONSTR_00001] [12]. Above expectation is needed in order to ensure that there is\nalways a software entity that can introduce changes in the current state of the\nMa-\nchine\n. If (for example) system integrator doesn’t configure\nState Management\nto\nbe started in\nStartup Machine State\n, then\nMachine\nwill never be able transit to\nany other state and will be stuck forever in it. This also applies to any other\nMachine\nState\nthat doesn’t have\nState Management\nconfigured.\nThe possibility that the\nMachine State\ntransition to the\nStartup\nstate is never\nreached shall be taken into account. In this case the\nState Management\ncan inter-\nrupt the\nStartup\nstate transition and request e.g. a recovery state using the\nara::\nexec::StateClient::SetState\ninterface. The\nara::exec::StateClient::\nGetIni…"

   "text": "Please note it is system integrator’s responsibility to carefully consider when system\nshutdown / restart should be requested because all\nProcesses\nwhich are still running\nwill not be terminated by\nExecution Management\n, which means that they will not be\nable to persist their data.\nAs mentioned in Section 7.4.2.1, AUTOSAR assumes that\nState Management\nwill\nbe configured to run in Shutdown and Restart. State transition is not a trivial system\nchange and it can fail for a number of reasons - in which case\nState Management\nshould remain alive to report errors and wait for further instructions. Please note that\nthe purpose of entering the Shutdown or Restart state is to shutdown or restart the\nMachine\n(this includes\nState Management\n) in a clean manner.\n[SWS_EM_02549] MachineFG.Off handling\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_EM_00101\n⌈\nExecution Management\nshall refuse a request to change\n\"MachineFG\" Func-\ntion Group State\nto\nOff\nwith error\nkI…"

Please\nnote that\nState Management\ncan repeat state transition request (to the same state)\nif previous transition ended with error. See Section 7.5\n7.1.1 Machine State\nA\nMachine State\nis a specific type of\nFunction Group State\n(see Section\n7.1.2).\nMachine States\nand all other\nFunction Group States\nare determined\nand requested by the\nState Management\nfunctional cluster, see Section 7.1.3. The\nset of active States is significantly influenced by vehiclewide events and modes which\nare evaluated into\nState Managements\ninternal States. A\nMachine State\nis a spe-\ncific type of\nFunction Group State\n(see Section 7.1.2).\nMachine States\nand all\nother\nFunction Group States\nare determined and requested by the\nState Man-\nagement\nfunctional cluster, see Section 7.1.3. The set of active States is significantly\ninfluenced by vehiclewide events and modes which are evaluated into\nState Man-\nagements\ninternal States.\nThe\nFunction Group States\n, including the\nMachine State\n, define the current\nset of running\nModelled Processe…"

Here, on receipt of the state change request,\nExecution Management\ntermi-\nnates running\nModelled Processes\nand then starts\nModelled Processes\nactive\nin the new state before confirming the state change to\nState Management\n."

   "text": "[SWS_SM_00031] Nested recovery handling\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00601\n⌈\nIn case of a nested recovery\nState Management\nshall provide the same result to\nall RecoveryHandler() calls related to the same affected\nStateMachine\nbased on\nthe result when the latest recovery action issued by the last RecoveryHandler() call is\nfinished.\n⌋\nNote: A \"nested recovery\" is very project specific and therefore an implementation\ndetail. For\nStateMachine\napproach this detail is explained in chapter 7.7.5.\nNote:\nPlatform Health Management\nmonitors the return of the RecoveryHan-\ndler() with a configurable timeout. If\nState Management\ngives no response to Re-\ncoveryHandler()\nPlatform Health Management\nwill do its own countermeasures\nby triggering or stop triggering the serviced watchdog.\nIf\nState Management\nis used in Safety Critical Platform, then it is suggested to\nuse Alive/Logical/Deadline supervision(s) and report their checkpoints appropriatel…"

   "text": "[SWS_SM_00210] Active update session\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nThe period between accepting an update session [SWS_SM_00631] and ending an\nupdate session [SWS_SM_00646] is considered by\nState Management\nas \"active\nupdate session\".\n⌋\nAs soon as\nState Management\nallows updating, it is necessary that\nState Man-\nagement\ndenies any further request for a new update session. To assure a higher\nconsistency in the\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\n, multiple update sessions at a\ntime shall be not allowed.\nFor the\nStateMachine\napproach a separate interface\nUpdateAllowed\nis provided\nto check if an update is allowed or not. This interface was introduced, because the lim-\nited logic of the\nStateMachine\nis not able to decide if an update is allowed.    "text": "Additionally\nState Management\nhas to persist the information about an ongoing up-\ndate session, thus, after a machine restart (independently if restart was expected or\nnot),\nUpdate and Configuration Management\ncan continue to update. To con-\ntinue the update in a consistent way it will be needed that only a few\nFunction\nGroups\nwill be set to a meaningful\nFunction Group State\n(project specific). At\nleast\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nhas to be in a running state.\n[SWS_SM_00204] Persist session status\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00004\n⌈\nState Management\nshall persist information about ongoing update session, thus it\ncan be read out after any kind of\nMachine\nreset.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00213] UpdateRequest method call rejection\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00004\n⌈\nA call to\nPrepareUpdate\n,\nVerifyUpdate\n,\nPrepareRollback\nor\nStopUpdate-\nSession\nshall return\nkOperationRejected\nif invoked outside an active update ses-\nsion.\n⌋\nPlease note tha…"

If and when the steps are done depends ad-\nditionally on the success or fail of the previous steps. For\nState Management\nthis means a transition to the ContinueUpdate\nstate for the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\n. However, the\nUpdate and Con-\nfiguration Management\nand the\nState Management\nneed to synchronize again.\nFor this reason the result of the\nResetMachine\nrequest is connected to a notification\nmechanism, which can be traced by the\nUpdate and Configuration Manage-\nment\n.\n[SWS_SM_00211] ResetMachine notification\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00004\n⌈\nState Management\nshall provide the service interface\nUpdateRequest\nto\nUpdate\nand Configuration Management\nwith the field\nResetMachineNotifier\nthus it\ncan trace the status from the\nResetMachine\ncall during and after it is pe…"

   "text": "How interaction between\nNetwork Management\nand\nState Management\nis han-\ndled when using\nStateMachine\napproach is shown in section 7.7.10 and in section\n7.7.5.\n7.5 Interaction with Suspend-to-RAM Functionality\nTo optimize the shutdown and startup times, the machine could use\nSuspend-to-\nRAM\ninstead of a complete shutdown and initial boot.\nThis includes before the OS is entering any suspend state\n• a (partial) shutdown of all\nFunction Groups\nincluding\nExecutables\nwhere\nExecutable\n.\nsuspendToRamAwareness\nis set to\nsuspendToRamNotSup-\nported\n. This means that either all affected\nFunction Groups\nare in \"Off\"\nstate, or at least in a state where these affected\nProcesss\nare not included/exe-\ncuted anymore.\n• a notification to all\nProcesss\nwhere their\nExecutable\n.\nsuspendToRamAware-\nness\nis set to\nsuspendToRamAware\n.    "text": "Figure 7.5: Interactions with StateMachine\nStateMachines\nare an optional element of\nState Management\n, so projects can\ndecide to implement\nState Management\nfully by its own. In this case, imple-\nmentation is not bound by requirements in Chapter\n7.7.\nThis is achieved by\nkeeping interfaces towards\nState Management\npublic.\n7.7.2 Controlling application for StateMachine States\nAs\nState Management\nshall not contain any project-specific logic (under which con-\ndition a\nStateMachine State\nis requested) it is assumed that a project-specific"

   "text": "and therefore there is no need to force the creation and offering of their respective\nStateMachineNotification\nservice interfaces.\n[SWS_SM_00618] StateMachine service interfaces - Offer\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nEach configured ara::com based service (\nStateMachineService\n,\nStateMachi-\nneNotification\n) for the\nStateMachine\nto be started shall be available (offered)\nwhen the\nActionListItem\n\"StartStateMachine\" is processed successfully.\n⌋\nPlease note that see [SWS_SM_00618] allows the\nSMControlApplication\nthe pos-\nsibility to request a new\nStateMachine State\ntransition immediately after the suc-\ncessful\nStateMachine\ncreation, even if the\nStateMachine\nis processing the initial\nActionList\n.\n[SWS_SM_00619] StateMachine service interfaces - StopOffer\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nEach configured ara::com based service (\nStateMachineService\n,\nStateMachi-\nneNotification\n) for a\nStateMachine\nshal…"

Therefore\nit is needed that\nAgent\ndo not manage\nFunction Groups\nwhich are claimed by\ndifferent\nSoftware Clusters\n.\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00018] Limitations of managed FunctionGroups\n⌈\nStateMachines\nin the role\nAgent\nshall only manage\nFunction Groups\nfrom the\nsame set of claimedFunctionGroups.\n⌋"

   "page": 48,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00024] Existence of StateMachine Off state\n⌈\nEach config-\nured\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nshall have corresponding \"Off\"\nStateMachine\nState\nconfigured, at the time when the creation of the manifest is finished.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00011] ActionListItems allowed in the \"Off\" state of a\nStateMachine of type Agent\n⌈\nIn the\nActionList\nreferencing the \"Off\" State of a\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\n, only the following\nActionListItems\nshall be al-\nlowed:\n•\nFunction Group\n::\nOff\n•\nNmNetworkHandle\n::\nNoCom\n•\nSYNC\n•\nSleep\n⌋\nIt is recommended that any\nStateMachine State\nfrom the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\ncontaining MachineFG::Shutdown or MachineFG::Restart should stop\nall\nStateMachines\nof type\nAgent\n. By not doing so, the still running processes would\nbe abruptly terminated when host is shut down.\nTo keep a consistent\nFunction Group State\nit is needed, that no\nFunction\nGroup\nis controlled by different\nStateMachines\n, as it wo…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P48_073",
   "page": 48,
   "text": "Figure 7.11: Function Group controlled by single StateMachine\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00013] Function Group shall only be controlled by single\nStateMachine\n⌈\nA\nFunction Group\nshall only be referenced by\nActionListItems\nof exactly one\nStateMachine\n.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P49_074",
   "page": 49,
   "text": "7.7.5 StateMachine state changes\nWhen a request to change a\nStateMachine State\nis issued by a\nSMControlAp-\nplication\nthere are more steps to consider:\n[SWS_SM_00605] StateMachine service interface RequestTransition - recovery\nongoing\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nThe\nRequestTransition\nmethod shall return\nkRecoveryTransitionOngoing\nif internal flag is set that error recovery is ongoing (see [SWS_SM_00601]) and shall\ncease any further processing of the request.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P50_075",
   "page": 50,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00603] StateMachine service interface RequestTransition - not al-\nlowed transition\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nThe\nRequestTransition\nmethod shall return\nkTransitionNotAllowed\nif the\ncurrent state of the\nStateMachine\nis not configured for the\nTransitionRequest\nvalue in\nTransitionRequestTable\nand shall cease any further processing of the\nrequest.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00604] StateMachine service interface RequestTransition - invalid\ntransition\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nThe\nRequestTransition\nmethod shall return\nkInvalidValue\nif\nTransition-\nRequest\nvalue is not configured in\nTransitionRequestTable\nand shall cease any\nfurther processing of the request.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00606] Canceling ongoing state transition of StateMachine\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIf transition request was accepted,\nRequestTransition\nmethod shall return\nkOp-\nerationCanceled\nto previous\nRequestTransition\nreq…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P51_076",
   "page": 51,
   "text": "Figure 7.13: StateMachine change\n[SWS_SM_00650] StateMachine service interface RequestTransition - transition\nfailed\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nThe\nRequestTransition\nmethod shall return\nkTransitionFailed\n, if an error\noccurred during processing of\nActionListItems\n(see [SWS_SM_00607]).\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P52_078",
   "page": 52,
   "text": "Figure 7.14: Extended transition request table\n[SWS_SM_00620] StateMachine transition - NetworkHandle goes to FullCom\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005, RS_SM_00401\n⌈\nWhen\nStateMachine\nreceives a change of a\nNetworkHandles\nto\nFullCom\nit shall\n• evaluate the next\nStateMachine State\nconfigured for TransitionRequest value\nand current state from\nTransitionRequestTable\n• stop processing\nActionListItems\nfrom the\nActionList\nreferencing the cur-\nrent\nStateMachine State\n• switch to the next\nStateMachine State\nimmediately and start processing\nActionListItems\nfrom the\nActionList\nreferencing this\nStateMachine\nState\n.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00621] StateMachine transition - NetworkHandle goes to NoCom\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005, RS_SM_00401\n⌈\nWhen\nStateMachine\nreceives a change of a\nNetworkHandles\nto\nNoCom\nit shall\n• evaluate the next\nStateMachine State\nconfigured for TransitionRequest value\nand current state from\nTransiti…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P54_080",
   "page": 54,
   "text": "• SYNC to sync between different\nActionListItems\n(corresponding to\nState-\nManagementSyncActionItem\n)\n• Sleep to delay processing the next\nActionListItems\n(corresponding to State-\nManagementSleepActionItem)\n• SetNetworkHandle switches the provided\nNetworkHandle\nto the configured\nstate (\nNoCom\nor\nFullCom\n) (corresponding to StateManagementNmActionItem)\n• EnterSuspendToRam used for requesting\nS2R-Aware applications\nto pre-\npare for\nSuspend-to-RAM\n(corresponding to StateManagementEnterSuspend-\nToRamActionItem)\n• EnterSuspendToRamOS used to request the OS to enter in\nSuspend-to-RAM\n(corresponding to StateManagementEnterSuspendToRamOsActionItem)\n• LeaveSuspendToRam used for requesting\nS2R-Aware applications\nto leave\ntheir\nSuspend-to-RAM\nstate (corresponding to StateManagementLeaveSus-\npendToRamActionItem)\n[SWS_SM_00608] ActionListItem - Function Group State\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen a Function Group State\nAc…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P55_081",
   "page": 55,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00611] processing ActionListItem\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nSubsequent\nActionListItems\nshall be processed in parallel unless SYNC\nAc-\ntionListItem\nis processed.\n⌋\nIn order to ensure that an\nActionList\nis fully processed, an implicit SYNC command\nis assumed at the end of every\nActionList\n.\n[SWS_SM_00667] Finalization of ActionList processing\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nAn\nActionList\nis successfully processed as soon as all\nActionListItems\n, con-\nfigured for the current\nActionList\n, have been executed and all results have been\ncollected.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P57_082",
   "page": 57,
   "text": "Figure 7.17: Arbitrary order for ActionListItems\nTo ensure that no\nFunction Group\nnor any\nNmNetworkHandle\nis missed in any\nstate, as it might lead to inconsistencies in the expected functionality, it is needed\nwithin a single\nStateMachine\n, that each\nActionList\ncontains the same\nFunc-\ntion Groups\nand\nNmNetworkHandle\ns, even if their state does not change from a\nStateMachine State\nto another.\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00015] Completeness of controlled Function Groups\n⌈\nEach\nActionList\nreferencing different\nStateMachine States\nof the same\nStateMa-\nchine\nshall reference the same set of\nFunction Groups\n.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P58_083",
   "page": 58,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00032] Completeness of controlled NmNetworkHandles\n⌈\nEach\nActionList\nreferencing different\nStateMachine States\nof the same\nStateMachine\nshall reference the same set of\nNmNetworkHandle\ns.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P58_084",
   "page": 58,
   "text": "Figure 7.18: Completeness of controlled Function Groups\n7.7.8 Controlling multiple StateMachine Instances\nThe\nActionListItem\napproach offers the ability to start/stop\nStateMachine\nin-\nstances, as it might be needed in a project-specific environment.\nTo reduce complexity in configuration there should be only one level of\nStateMachine\nnesting. Therefore, only the\nStateMachine\nwith the role\nController\nshould be\nused to Start/Stop other\nStateMachine\ninstances, called\nAgents\n.\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00019] Usage of ActionListItem \"StartStateMachine\" and\n\"StopStateMachine\"\n⌈\nOnly the\nStateMachine\nwith the role\nController\nshall use\nthe\nActionListItem\n\"StartStateMachine\" and \"StopStateMachine\".\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P59_085",
   "page": 59,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00016] Completeness of controlled StateMachines\n⌈\nEach\nActionList\nreferencing a\nStateMachine State\nof a\nStateMachines\nof type\nController\n, shall reference the complete set of\nAgents\nthat are controlled by the\nController\n.\n⌋\nThe process of starting a\nStateMachine\nis a protracted operation that involves mul-\ntiple steps. On the one hand, the configured interfaces, such as the\nStateMachi-\nneService\nand the\nStateMachineNotification\n, associated with the specific\nStateMachine\nmust be initialized and provided to ensure that the\nStateMachine\nis accessible from the application layer. On the other hand, the\nStateMachine\nitself\nmust initiate the processing of the\nActionList\nthat corresponds to the requested ini-\ntial\nStateMachine State\n. This processing is governed by the specifications outlined\nin [SWS_SM_00612] or [SWS_SM_00622].\nFrom the perspective of the\nController\n, a\nStateMachine\nis considered started\nonce it exists an…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P60_086",
   "page": 60,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00623] ActionListItem \"Start StateMachine\" - with parameter, StateMa-\nchine is already running\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen the\nActionListItem\n\"Start StateMachine\" is processed, and the referenced\nStateMachine\nis already started, the\nStateMachine\nshall transition to the state,\nwhich is provided as parameter.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P62_087",
   "page": 62,
   "text": "Please note that all\nActionListItems\nof a requested\nStateMachine State\nwill always be executed, independently if the\nStateMachine\nwas already in the\nrequested\nStateMachine State\ndirectly before the request. This is valid for\n[SWS_SM_00623], [SWS_SM_00620], [SWS_SM_00621], [SWS_SM_00601] and\n[SWS_SM_00607]."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P62_088",
   "page": 62,
   "text": "Figure 7.20: StartStateMachine decision tree\n[SWS_SM_00614] ActionListItem \"Stop StateMachine\" processing\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nAt the end of the processing of StopStateMachine\nActionListItem\n, the referenced\nStateMachine\nshall cease to exist.\n⌋\nDuring update session StateManagement needs to prepare parts of\nMachine\nfor\nupdate. [SWS_SM_00614] together with [SWS_SM_00619] and [SWS_SM_00651]\nserves an important role here. They ensure that, when StopStateMachine is executed,\nthe\nStateMachine\nis in a state where it could be safely updated by\nUpdate and\nConfiguration Management\n.\n[SWS_SM_00615] ActionListItem \"Stop StateMachine\" processing - StateMa-\nchine is not running\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen the\nActionListItem\n\"Stop StateMachine\" is processed, and the\nStateMa-\nchine\nwith the provided ID is not running, this processing shall be skipped.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P63_089",
   "page": 63,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00651] Processing StopStateMachine ActionListItem\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nDuring the processing of\nActionListItem\n\"StopStateMachine\" the referenced\nStateMachine\nshall be transitioned to the \"Off\"\nStateMachine State\n.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P63_090",
   "page": 63,
   "text": "Figure 7.21: Processing ActionListItem StopStateMachine\nPlease note, that only\nStateMachines\nof type\nAgent\nneed an \"Off\"\nStateMachine\nState\n. This is needed to ensure that, no processes or\nNmNetworkHandle\ns are left\n\"uncontrolled\" when the\nStateMachine\nis being stopped (see [SWS_SM_00614]).\nFrom the\nController\nperspective a stopped\nStateMachine\nmeans that the\nStateMachine\ndoes no longer exist. Therefore waiting that the Off State is reached\nand the configured interfaces from the\nAgent\nare no longer provided is mandatory"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P64_091",
   "page": 64,
   "text": "(see Figure: Processing ActionListItem StopStateMachine and [SWS_SM_00651]). A\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nis representing life-cycle of a\nMachine\n. For this\nreason stopping a\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshould consider usage of\nMa-\nchineFG Shutdown\nstate. The name of\nStateMachine State\nwhich is performing\nthis task does not need to be standardized as the\nState Management\ndoes not intent\nto shutdown\nMachine\non its own.\n7.7.9 ActionListItem Sleep\nTo support timed actions of\nStateMachine States\ne.g. to realize \"afterrun use-\ncases\" the\nSleep ActionListItem\nwas introduced.\n[SWS_SM_00624] ActionListItem - Sleep\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen a\nSleep ActionListItem\nis found in the\nActionLists\n,\nStateMachine\nshall delay processing next\nActionListItem\non the\nActionLists\nfor the config-\nured time.\n⌋\nPlease note that\nSleep ActionListItem\nwill not \"block\" processing incoming trig-\ngers meanwhile. This means t…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P65_092",
   "page": 65,
   "text": "7.7.10 ActionListItem SetNetworkHandle\nTo support switching of NetworkHandles within\nStateMachine States\nthe\nSet-\nNetworkHandle ActionListItem\nwas introduced. To make this work a mapping\nSmInteractsWithNmMapping\nbetween\nNmNetworkHandle\nand\nStateManage-\nmentNmActionItem\nhas to be configured.\n[SWS_SM_00625] ActionListItem - SetNetworkHandle FullCom\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005, RS_SM_00401\n⌈\nWhen a\nSetNetworkHandle ActionListItem\nwith parameter\nFullCom\nis found\nin the\nActionLists\n,\nStateMachine\nshall set the corresponding NetworkHandle to\nFullCom\n.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00626] ActionListItem - SetNetworkHandle NoCom\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005, RS_SM_00401\n⌈\nWhen a\nSetNetworkHandle ActionListItem\nwith parameter\nNoCom\nis found in\nthe\nActionLists\n,\nStateMachine\nshall set the corresponding NetworkHandle to\nNoCom\n.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P66_093",
   "page": 66,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00025] NmNetworkHandle shall only be controlled by sin-\ngle StateMachine\n⌈\nA\nNmNetworkHandle\nshall only be referenced by\nActionLis-\ntItems\nof exactly one\nStateMachine\n.\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P66_094",
   "page": 66,
   "text": "Figure 7.24: StateMachine to NmNetworkHandle restriction\n7.7.11 StateMachine State notification\nAs\nState Management StateMachine States\nreflect the current functionality of\na\nMachine\n, which might be in the interest of several entities in the\nMachine\n(e.g. Fire-\nwall, SystemHealthManagement, ...) it shall be possible to make the\nStateMachine\nStates\navailable to them. Therefore, it shall be possible to configure a\nStateMachi-\nneNotification\nservice interface (modelled as meta-class\nServiceInterface\n)\nfor a\nStateMachine\n."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P67_095",
   "page": 67,
   "text": "Figure 7.25: Value of configured StateMachineNotification::CurrentState field\n[SWS_SM_00616] CurrentState value during StateMachine State transition\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen a\nStateMachineNotification\ninterface is configured for the\nStateMa-\nchine\nand a\nStateMachine State\ntransition has been started, the value of the\nCurrentState\nfield shall be set to \"inTransition\".\n⌋\nPlease note that the value \"inTransition\" is set independently of the source (\nPlatform\nHealth Management\n,\nExecution Management\n,\nSMControlApplication\n, ...)\nand is kept, even if another\nStateMachine State\ntransition, as reaction to an er-\nror notification, is performed.\n[SWS_SM_00617] CurrentState value after StateMachine State transition\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen a\nStateMachineNotification\ninterface is configured for the\nStateMa-\nchine\nthe value of the\nCurrentState\nfield shall be set to the current\nStateM…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P68_097",
   "page": 68,
   "text": "Figure 7.26: ActionList timeout\n[SWS_SM_00668] Default value for ActionListTimeout\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen\nStateManagementActionList\n.\nmaxActionListDuration\nis not config-\nured,\nState Management\nshall use\nStateManagementModuleInstantiation\n.\nmaxActionListDuration\n(aka the global\nActionListTimeout\n).\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00669] ActionList timeout monitoring\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nState Management\nshall monitor the time required to process the\nActionList\n(the time between processing the first\nActionListItem\nand receiving the last re-\nsponse associated with\nActionList\n(see [SWS_SM_00667]).\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P69_099",
   "page": 69,
   "text": "Figure 7.27: ErrorRecoveryTable\nTo ensure that all errors are covered the following constraint is needed:\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014] Handling of non-mapped ErrorCode\n⌈\nEach\nError-\nRecoveryTable\nshall have exactly one entry configured with value ANY as the Error-\nCode.\n⌋\nThe ANY entry will be used to change to the configured\nStateMachine State\nwhen\na not configured ErrorCode is reported by\nPlatform Health Management\n,\nExe-\ncution Management\nor\nState Management\nitself.\nDuring an active update session, handling of the recovery actions (see\n[SWS_SM_00601] and [SWS_SM_00664]) should be treated differently, depending on\nwhether the\nStateMachine\nitself is \"ImpactedByUpdate\" [SWS_SM_00654] or not.\nOtherwise errors occurred during or after methods called by the\nUpdate and Con-\nfiguration Management\ncould result in\nStateMachines\ntransiting to recovery\nStateMachine State\n, which might not be the intended action.\n[SWS_SM_00601] StateMachine error…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P70_100",
   "page": 70,
   "text": "• stop processing\nActionListItems\nfrom the\nActionList\nreferencing the cur-\nrent\nStateMachine State\n• switch to the next\nStateMachine State\nimmediately and start processing\nActionListItems\nfrom the\nActionList\nreferencing this\nStateMachine\nState\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00666] Nested recovery\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00601\n⌈\nIn case that a new issue is reported and the issue has to be handled by a\nStateMa-\nchine\nwhere internal flag ErrorRecoveryOngoing is set (see [SWS_SM_00601]), this\nshall be considered as \"nested recovery\" (see [SWS_SM_00031]).\n⌋"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P72_101",
   "page": 72,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00602] StateMachine ErrorRecoveryOngoing flag reset\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nThe internal flag that error recovery is ongoing, shall be reset, when all\nActionLis-\ntItems\nof an\nActionList\nreferencing a\nStateMachine State\n, which is requested\ndue to error reaction, are successfully processed.\n⌋\nThe following list presents an overview of the errors, which can be detected and han-\ndled by StateManagement:\n• Errors reported by\nPlatform Health Management\nor\nExecution Manage-\nment\ndue to a detected failure at\nProcess\nlevel (see [SWS_SM_00670]).\n• Errors reported by ara::exec::StateClient related to failed or invalid requests as\nwell as ara::exec::StateClient communication issues (see [SWS_SM_00671]).\n• Errors at\nStateMachine\ntransitions, where processing the complete\nAction-\nList\noverpassed the specified timeout (see [SWS_SM_00673]).\n• Errors detected when a\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nfails to start or to…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P73_102",
   "page": 73,
   "text": "The first case will return the mapped ExecutionError from the failed process and a\nrecovery action can be performed (see [SWS_SM_00670]). For the second case the\nErrorCode\nfunctionGroupTransitionRequestFailedError\nmapped to\nFunc-\ntionGroupErrorMapping\ncan be configured.\n[SWS_SM_00671] ErrorCode as reaction to a failed SetState request\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIf the SetState error is \"ara::exec::ExecErrc::kNoCommunication\",\n\"ara::exec::ExecErrc::kInvalidTransition\" or \"ara::exec::ExecErrc::kInvalidMetaModelIdentifier\"\nthe configured\nfunctionGroupTransitionRequestFailedError\nmapped to\nFunctionGroupErrorMapping\nshall be used as ErrorCode in the\nStateMachine\nwhich manages the affected\nFunction Group\n.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00672] Default value for functionGroupTransitionRequestFailedError\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIn case\nfunctionGroupTransitionRequestFailedError\ndoes n…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P74_103",
   "page": 74,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00674] Default value for StateManagementAction-\nList.maxDurationExceededError\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIn case\nmaxDurationExceededError\ndoes not have an ErrorCode configured,\nState Management\nshall use the ErrorCode value 1.\n⌋\nIf a\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nfails to be started or stopped by the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\n, a recovery action is needed. Please note that these errors refer\nto the process of creating and destroying the\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nas well\nas its service interfaces, and not about errors during processing the\nActionLists\nmapped to the InitialMode and Off States from the\nStateMachine\n. In order to con-\nfigure these kind of errors the\nstartAgentError\nand\nstopAgentError\nmapped to\nthe\nStateMachine\nitself will be used.\n[SWS_SM_00675] ErrorCode for failed creation of a StateMachine of type Agent\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P75_104",
   "page": 75,
   "text": "When a\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\ndetects an error, a recovery action will be\nstarted based on the\nAgent\n’s\nErrorRecoveryTable\n. Usually those errors are han-\ndled in the\nAgent\n’s scope and are not visible to the\nStateMachine\nof type\nCon-\ntroller\n. Sometimes however a successful processing of an\nActionList\n, associ-\nated with an\nAgent StateMachine State\n, can be important enough that, any error\ndetected during the execution of the mentioned\nActionList\n, should be signaled back\nto the\nController\n. In this case the\nactionListProcessingFailedError\ncan be\nused.\n[SWS_SM_00679] ErrorCode for failure during processing of an Agent ActionList\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIf the processing of the\nAgent ActionList\nresulted in a failure and\nactionList-\nProcessingFailedError\nis configured for that\nActionList\n, then\nactionList-\nProcessingFailedError\nshall be used as ErrorCode in the\nController Error-\nRecoveryT…"
  },

   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P76_105",
   "page": 76,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00687] ErrorCode for failed LeaveSuspendToRam\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005, RS_SM_00402\n⌈\nIf the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\ndetects an error when processing the\nLeaveSuspendToRam\nActionListItem\n, the configured\nleaveSuspendToRamEr-\nror\nshall be used as ErrorCode in the\nController\n’s\nErrorRecoveryTable\n.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00688] Default value for leaveSuspendToRamError\nStatus:\nDRAFT\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005, RS_SM_00402\n⌈\nIn case\nleaveSuspendToRamError\ndoes not have an ErrorCode configured,\nState\nManagement\nshall use the ErrorCode value 1.\n⌋"

   "text": "Figure 7.29: Overview for the StateMachine ErrorCodes handling\n7.7.14 StateMachine support for Update and Configuration Management\nTo support\nUpdate and Configuration Management\n[10] during\nMachine\nup-\ndate,\nState Management\nprovides\nUpdateRequest\ninterface. In general, update"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P79_108",
   "page": 79,
   "text": "Figure 7.31: Overview of update session within StateMachine approach (part 2 of 2)\nThe\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nexpects that a single logical en-\ntity will be responsible for\nStateMachine\nduring update session. For this reason it\nis needed to restrict who can instantiate\nUpdateRequest\ninterface and how many\ninstances are permitted per\nMachine\n.\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020] Upper Multiplicity of UpdateRequest interface\n⌈\nIn the\ncontext of a\nMachine\n, there shall be at most one Port typed by the\nUpdateRequest\ninterface.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00629] Only Process controlling StateMachine of type Controller can\nprovide UpdateRequest interface\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIf a\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nhas a\nPort configured that is typed by the\nUpdateRequest\ninterface, it shall instantiate\nUpdateRequest\ninterface.\n⌋\nMachine\nupdate starts with\nUpdate and Configuration Management\ncalling\nReq…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P80_109",
   "page": 80,
   "text": "UpdateAllowed\naccordingly. Please note that it is expected the feasibility of an up-\ndate campaign should be assessed at the vehicle level and\nUpdate and Configu-\nration Management\nis not expected to call\nRequestUpdateSession\nwithout up-\nfront synchronization. However, update campaign may involve multiple\nMachines\nand\ntherefore take some time. During this time local circumstances may change and for\nthis reason call to\nRequestUpdateSession\nis necessary.\nWhen\nSMControlApplication\ndoes not allow update,\nModelled Process\ncon-\ntrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshould refuse update request from\nUp-\ndate and Configuration Management\n.\n[SWS_SM_00630] Rejection of update session\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen\nUpdateAllowed\nis set to\nkUpdateNotAllowed\n,\nModelled Process\ncon-\ntrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshall return\nkOperationRejected\ner-\nror from the\nRequestUpdateSession\nmethod.\n⌋\nIf\nSMControlAppl…"
  },

   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P81_110",
   "page": 81,
   "text": "Figure 7.32: Requesting update session within StateMachine approach\nPlease note that it is deliberately left as an implementation detail when\nRequestTran-\nsition\nmethod should be blocked.\nAUTOSAR Adaptive Platform\nwill only specify\nthe latest point in time when this should happen. Implementations may choose to keep\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nmore responsive, by accepting state change re-\nquests, in case there is a delay between calling\nRequestUpdateSession\nand actual\nstart of the update process.\n[SWS_SM_00654] StateMachine marked as \"ImpactedByUpdate\"\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nDuring a call to\nPrepareUpdate\n,\nVerifyUpdate\nor\nPrepareRollback\n, the\nMod-\nelled Process\ncontrolling the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshall mark a"
  },

   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P82_111",
   "page": 82,
   "text": "StateMachine\nas \"ImpactedByUpdate\", if any of the\nFunction Groups\nmanaged\nby the\nStateMachine\nis listed in the parameter passed to the method call.\n⌋\nBecause the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nmanages also the\nStateMa-\nchines\nof type\nAgent\n, the\nController\nis also affected by update session when\na\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nis marked \"ImpactedByUpdate\".\n[SWS_SM_00655] Indirect marking of StateMachine of type Controller as \"Im-\npactedByUpdate\"\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhenever a\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nis marked as \"ImpactedByUpdate\" the\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshall also be marked as \"ImpactedByUpdate\".\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00664] StateMachine error reaction of StateMachines \"ImpactedByUp-\ndate\"\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nWhen ExecutionErrorEvent::executionError is reported from\nPlatform Health\nManagement\nor from\nExecution Management\nand the\nStateMachine\nis \"Impact-\nedByUpdate\" [SWS…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P83_112",
   "page": 83,
   "text": "Configuration Management\nneeds exclusive access to the\nMachine\nand\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\ncan not only command\nFunction Groups\n,\nbut also others\nStateMachines\n, it should prevent any further changes to its own\nStateMachine State\nto avoid a situation where, for example, a\nFunction Group\nis at the same time updated and activated.\nPlease note that once a call to\nRequestTransition\nof\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nhas been answered with\nkUpdateInProgress\n, each consecutive call\nshould be answered with\nkUpdateInProgress\n, until\nUpdate and Configura-\ntion Management\ncalls\nStopUpdateSession\n(see [SWS_SM_00647]).\nTo enable a\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nto fulfill all steps which are needed during\nan update session it is needed that the\nStateMachine State\ncannot be influenced\nfrom the outside if they are marked as \"ImpactedByUpdate\".\n[SWS_SM_00649] Block RequestTransition method during an update session\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_S…"

   "text": "[SWS_SM_00634] Shutdown of affected StateMachines during a call to Prepare-\nUpdate method\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\n, during a\ncall to\nPrepareUpdate\nmethod, shall stop every affected\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\n.\n⌋\nPlease note that it is expected that [SWS_SM_00634] is only executed after a success-\nful execution of [SWS_SM_00633] for a particular\nStateMachine\n.\nStopping an\nStateMachine\neffectively transition all\nFunction Groups\nmanaged\nby that\nStateMachine\n, to the\nOff\nstate. For this reason a transition to the\nOff\nstate in [SWS_SM_CONSTR_00021] is not mandatory, but can be performed for clarity\nreasons.\nIf any of the steps required to prepare for update fails,\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshould return an error to\nUpdate and Con-\nfiguration Management\n. For example, a transition of affected\nStateMachine\nto\nthe\nPrep…"

It is rec-\nommended that\nVerify\nstate, which is mandatory for every\nFunction Group\n, is\nused.\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00022] Existence of StateMachine VerifyUpdate state\n⌈\nEach\nconfigured\nStateMachine\nshall have corresponding\nVerifyUpdate StateMa-\nchine State\nconfigured, at the time when the creation of the manifest is finished.\n⌋\nBefore starting verification, it is needed to block\nRequestTransition\nmethod - when\nnot already done.\nAs the next step, transition of all affected\nStateMachines\nto the\nVerifyUpdate\nstate is needed. When identifying which\nStateMachines\nare affected, the list that\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nsupplies as a parameter to the\nVeri-\nfyUpdate\nmethod can be used.\n[SWS_SM_00638] Transition affected StateMachines to VerifyUpdate state\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nControl…"
  },

   "doc": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P85_115",
   "page": 85,
   "text": "Figure 7.33: Example for StateMachineState VerifyUpdate for an Agent\nFor the same reason it is needed that changes in\nNetworkHandles\nare not evaluated\nduring\nStateMachines\nof type\nAgent\nare in\nStateMachine State VerifyUp-\ndate\n.\nThis is only needed for\nStateMachine State VerifyUpdate\nand not for\nPre-\npareUpdate\nand\nPrepareRollback\n, as the corresponding\nStateMachine\nwill be\nstopped after these\nStateMachine States\n(see [SWS_SM_00634])."

   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P86_116",
   "page": 86,
   "text": "As\nStateMachine State\nof\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshould not\nchange during an \"active update session\" it is additionally needed, that its\nStateMa-\nchine State\ndoes not change when a\nNmNetworkHandle\nchanges.\n[SWS_SM_00628] Evaluation of NetworkHandle changes for StateMachine of\ntype Controller\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nshall keep its\nStateMachine State\n, when\nthe\nRequestTransition\nfor\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nreturns\nkUpdateIn-\nProgress\nand changes in a\nNmNetworkHandle\nare recognized.\n⌋\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nneeds to check\nthe result of all operations needed for verification. For example, if the\nVerifyUpdate\nstate for\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nrequires a\nFunction Group\nstate transi-\ntion and that transition is unsuccessful,\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\nshould pass\nthis information to the\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\no…"

   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P88_117",

   "text": "Figure 7.35: Verify and prepare rollback within StateMachine approach - part 2/2\n[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00023] Existence of StateMachine PrepareRollback state\n⌈\nEach configured\nStateMachine\nshall have\nPrepareRollback StateMachine\nState\nconfigured, at the time when the creation of the manifest is finished.\n⌋\nAfter this preparation for rollback can be started."

   "page": 89,
   "text": "[SWS_SM_00642] Transition affected StateMachines to PrepareRollback state\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\n, during a call\nto\nPrepareRollback\nmethod, shall transition every affected\nStateMachine\nto the\nPrepareRollback\nstate.\n⌋\n[SWS_SM_00643] Shutdown of affected StateMachines during a call to Pre-\npareRollback method\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\n, during a call\nto\nPrepareRollback\nmethod, shall stop every affected\nStateMachine\nof type\nAgent\n.\n⌋\nResult of the preparation for rollback should be communicated back to\nUpdate and\nConfiguration Management\n.\n[SWS_SM_00644] Failing to prepare for rollback\nUpstream requirements:\nRS_SM_00001, RS_SM_00005\n⌈\nIf\nModelled Process\ncontrolling\nStateMachine\nof type\nController\nfails to pre-\npare for the rollback process, it shall return\nkOpera…"

   "id": "SNIP_sm_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_S_P90_119",
