Suspend-to-RAM-Eintritts über S2RHub, Satelliten und Betriebssystemaufruf. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81110" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81110">[SWS_SM_81110]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81010" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81010">[SWS_SM_81010]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81112" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81112">[SWS_SM_81112]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=35">SWS StateManagement §7.5 „Interaction between S2RSatellite and S2RHub“</a></p> <h4>Interaktion mit Update and Configuration Management während Fahrzeug-Updates</h4> <p>Während Software-Aktualisierungen arbeitet das State Management eng mit dem Update and Configuration Management (UCM) zusammen (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=76">SWS StateManagement §7.7.14 „StateMachine support for Update and Configuration Management“</a>). Hierzu stellt das SM die Service-Schnittstelle <code>UpdateRequest</code> bereit (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91016" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91016">[SWS_SM_91016]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91017" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91017">[SWS_SM_91017]</a>). Im Kontext einer Machine darf exakt ein Port für diese Schnittstelle existieren (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020]</a>), der zwingend vom Prozess des <code>Controller</code> instanziiert werden muss (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00629" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00629">[SWS_SM_00629]</a>). Ob eine Aktualisierung zulässig ist, bestimmt die <code>SMControlApplication</code> über das Service-Feld <code>UpdateAllowed</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91108" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91108">[SWS_SM_91108]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=30">SWS StateManagement §7.4 „Update session“</a>). Ist dieses auf <code>kUpdateNotAllowed</code> gesetzt, weist das SM den Aufruf <code>RequestUpdateSession</code> mit <code>kOperationRejected</code> ab (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00630" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00630">[SWS_SM_00630]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91102" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91102">[SWS_SM_91102]</a>).</p> <p>Wird eine Update-Sitzung akzeptiert, gilt diese als aktiv (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00210" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00210">[SWS_SM_00210]</a>). Das SM persistiert diesen Zustand resilient, sodass er auch nach einem Reboot abrufbar bleibt (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00204" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00204">[SWS_SM_00204]</a>). Parallele Update-Sitzungen sind unzulässig (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00209" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00209">[SWS_SM_00209]</a>). Die Aktualisierung gliedert sich in methodische Schritte: Über <code>PrepareUpdate</code> übergibt das UCM eine Liste betroffener Funktionsgruppen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91103" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91103">[SWS_SM_91103]</a>). Das SM markiert die zugehörigen Agent-Zustandsmaschinen als <code>"ImpactedByUpdate"</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00654" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00654">[SWS_SM_00654]</a>), wodurch transitiv auch der Controller als <code>"ImpactedByUpdate"</code> gekennzeichnet wird (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00655" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00655">[SWS_SM_00655]</a>). Sämtliche betroffenen Agenten werden daraufhin gestoppt (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00634" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00634">[SWS_SM_00634]</a>), und normale Zustandswechselanfragen via <code>RequestTransition</code> werden mit <code>kUpdateInProgress</code> blockiert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00649" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00649">[SWS_SM_00649]</a>).</p> <p>Für die anschließende Prüfung muss jede Zustandsmaschine über einen modellierten Zustand <code>VerifyUpdate</code> verfügen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00022" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00022">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00022]</a>), der bei Aufruf von <code>VerifyUpdate</code> eingenommen wird (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00638" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00638">[SWS_SM_00638]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91104" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91104">[SWS_SM_91104]</a>). Für Rollback-Szenarien existiert analog der Pflichtzustand <code>PrepareRollback</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00023" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00023">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00023]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00642" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00642">[SWS_SM_00642]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91105" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91105">[SWS_SM_91105]</a>). Verlangt das UCM über <code>ResetMachine</code> einen Neustart (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91100" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91100">[SWS_SM_91100]</a>), wechselt der Controller in den Zustand <code>Restart</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00658" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00658">[SWS_SM_00658]</a>). Nach dem anschließenden Maschinenstart fährt das SM aufgrund der aktiven Update-Sitzung in den Zustand <code>ContinueUpdate</code> anstelle des regulären <code>Initial</code>-Zustands hoch (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00657" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00657">[SWS_SM_00657]</a>) und meldet den Status über das Feld <code>ResetMachineNotifier</code> an das UCM (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00662" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00662">[SWS_SM_00662]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91106" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91106">[SWS_SM_91106]</a>). Beendet wird die Sitzung über <code>StopUpdateSession</code>, woraufhin der Controller in den Zustand <code>AfterUpdate</code> übergeht (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00205" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00205">[SWS_SM_00205]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00646" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00646">[SWS_SM_00646]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91101" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91101">[SWS_SM_91101]</a>).</p> <h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall und Überwachungsreaktionen</h4> <p>Das Platform Health Management (PHM) überwacht Applikationen und meldet festgestellte Überwachungsfehler über den Callback <code>RecoveryHandler()</code> an das State Management (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture&amp;page=220">EXP SWArchitecture §11.1.2.2.1 „Scenario: Recover by System State Change“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture&amp;page=234">EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.2 „Scenario: Report Supervision Failure“</a>). Um auf Fehler reagieren zu können, muss sich das SM vorab über <code>Offer()</code> beim PHM registrieren (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture&amp;page=234">EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.2 „Scenario: Report Supervision Failure“</a>). Reagiert das SM nicht innerhalb des im Manifest konfigurierten Timeouts auf den <code>RecoveryHandler()</code>, eskaliert das PHM über <code>FireWatchdogReaction()</code> zu einem harten Maschinen-Reset (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture&amp;page=234">EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.2 „Scenario: Report Supervision Failure“</a>). Ebenso führt ein kritischer Fehler im SM-Prozess selbst direkt zur Watchdog-Auslösung (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture&amp;page=235">EXP SWArchitecture §11.5.1.3.1 „Scenario: Recover from Critical Supervision Failure in State Management“</a>).</p> <p>Im <code>StateMachine</code>-Ansatz wird die Fehlerbehebung über die <code>ErrorRecoveryTable</code> deklariert (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=69">SWS StateManagement §7.7.13 „ErrorRecoveryTable“</a>). Um lückenlose Fehlerabdeckung sicherzustellen, muss jede Fehlertabelle exakt einen Eintrag mit dem Fehlercode <code>ANY</code> aufweisen, der als Auffangregel für nicht explizit zugeordnete Fehler dient (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014]</a>). Sobald eine Fehlerreaktion initiiert wird, setzt die Zustandsmaschine das interne Flag <code>ErrorRecoveryOngoing</code>, bricht die laufende Aktionsliste ab und startet unmittelbar die Aktionsliste des Wiederherstellungszustands (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00601" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00601">[SWS_SM_00601]</a>). Das Flag bleibt aktiv und blockiert reguläre Übergänge, bis alle Aktionsschritte der Fehlerreaktion erfolgreich abgeschlossen sind (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00602" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00602">[SWS_SM_00602]</a>). Treten währenddessen weitere Fehler auf, greift die verschachtelte Fehlerbehandlung (<code>Nested Recovery</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00031" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00031">[SWS_SM_00031]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00666" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00666">[SWS_SM_00666]</a>). Meldet das SM dem PHM, dass es einen Fehler nicht beheben kann (Fehlercode <code>kSMCanNotHandleRecovery</code>), löst das PHM den Watchdog-Reset aus (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture&amp;page=220">EXP SWArchitecture §11.1.2.2.2 „Scenario: Recover by Watchdog Reset“</a>).</p> <div class="diagram" </g> </svg></div> <p class="diagram-note">Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklus und Verzweigung der Fehlerbehandlung mit ErrorRecoveryTable und Flag ErrorRecoveryOngoing. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00601" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00601">[SWS_SM_00601]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00602" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00602">[SWS_SM_00602]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=69">SWS StateManagement §7.7.13 „ErrorRecoveryTable“</a></p> <p>Fehler bei Schnittstellenaufrufen werden über die C++-Fehlerdomäne <code>SmErrorDomain</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81247" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81247">[SWS_SM_81247]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81251" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81251">[SWS_SM_81251]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_91010" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_91010">[SWS_SM_91010]</a>) mit dem Bezeichner <code>"Sm"</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81248" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81248">[SWS_SM_81248]</a>) abgebildet. Der Enumerator <code>SmErrc</code> definiert systemspezifische Fehlercodes wie <code>kOfferFailed</code> (Dienstangebot fehlgeschlagen) und <code>kCommunicationFailed</code> (Kommunikationsabbruch zu Satelliten) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81240" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81240">[SWS_SM_81240]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81244" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81244">[SWS_SM_81244]</a>). Im Ausnahmefall können diese Fehler über <code>ThrowAsException</code> als <code>SmException</code> geworfen werden, sofern C++-Exceptions in der Plattform aktiviert sind (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81243" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81243">[SWS_SM_81243]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81250" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81250">[SWS_SM_81250]</a>).</p> <h4>Weiterführende Detailbelege</h4> <p>Die normative Basis des Moduls State Management stützt sich auf folgende zentrale Spezifikationsanker:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Prozess- und Zustandssteuerung:</strong> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00400" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00400">[SWS_SM_00400]</a> verankert die Nutzung der <code>StateClient</code>-API gegenüber dem Execution Management; <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00017" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00017">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00017]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00019" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00019">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00019]</a> definieren die Alleinstellung des <code>Controller</code> für <code>MachineFG</code> und die Agent-Steuerung (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=46">SWS StateManagement §7.7.4</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_ExecutionManagement&amp;page=62">SWS ExecutionManagement §7.4.5</a>).</li> <li><strong>Aktionslisten und Synchronisation:</strong> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00608" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00608">[SWS_SM_00608]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00611" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00611">[SWS_SM_00611]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00667" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00667">[SWS_SM_00667]</a> regeln die parallele Ausführung von Aktionslistenelementen und die Synchronisationspunkte über <code>SYNC</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=54">SWS StateManagement §7.7.7</a>).</li> <li><strong>Fehlerbehandlung und Resilienz:</strong> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00014]</a> fordert den lückenlosen <code>ANY</code>-Fallback in Fehlertabellen; <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00601" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00601">[SWS_SM_00601]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00602" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00602">[SWS_SM_00602]</a> steuern das Sperrflag während aktiver Fehlerreaktionen (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=69">SWS StateManagement §7.7.13</a>).</li> <li><strong>Fahrzeug-Update (UCM):</strong> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020">[SWS_SM_CONSTR_00020]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00204" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00204">[SWS_SM_00204]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00210" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00210">[SWS_SM_00210]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00657" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00657">[SWS_SM_00657]</a> sichern die exklusive Instanziierung des <code>UpdateRequest</code>-Ports, die Persistierung von Update-Sitzungen und den Start in <code>ContinueUpdate</code> nach einem Reboot (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=31">SWS StateManagement §7.4</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=79">SWS StateManagement §7.7.14</a>).</li> <li><strong>Schnellstart (Suspend-to-RAM):</strong> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00701" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00701">[SWS_SM_00701]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_00714" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_00714">[SWS_SM_00714]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81110" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81110">[SWS_SM_81110]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_SM_81112" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_SM_81112">[SWS_SM_81112]</a> normieren die IAM-gesicherte Orchestrierung von Satelliten und die OS-Übergabe über den <code>S2RHub</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_StateManagement&amp;page=35">SWS StateManagement §7.5.1</a>).</li> </ul> <!-- annahmen: 1) Interpretation: Das Vorhandensein eines standardisierten MachineFG-Zustands Restart neben Shutdown und Startup legt nahe, dass SM im Controller-Zustand Restart gezielt Persistierungs- und Aufräumroutinen vor dem Reboot orchestriert. – Begründung: Der Payload beschreibt den Übergang in Restart im Rahmen von ResetMachine, spezifiziert die hardwarenahe Reboot-Auslösung jedoch als Aufgabe der Plattform bzw. des OS. 2) Interpretation: Das Verbot FG-übergreifender Execution Dependencies wird im State Management typischerweise über separate StateMachine-Agenten und deren sequenzierte Transitionen durch den Controller aufgelöst. – Begründung: SWS_EM_CONSTR_00013 und SWS_EM (S. 43/65) verbieten FG-übergreifende Abhängigkeiten im Manifest und verweisen für die Orchestrierung auf State Management. --> <p class="ai-note">Dieser Leitfaden wurde durch einen KI-Kurations-Assistenten auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikationen für Release R25-11 erstellt.</p> </div>

Architecture handling low-level middleware. The AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform demands that the Watchdog is enabled prior to the startup of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform, for ex- ample, the Watchdog could already be enabled by the Bootloader or the Operat- ing System . Execution Management is started by the Operating System as the first process of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Execution Management then controls the startup of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform by activating the standardized Function Group State called Startup of the Machine Function Group State . This trig- gers the start of additional processes that are configured to run in the Startup state. It is mandatory that State Management is part of the Startup state. Other processes of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform, for example Platform Health Management and application processes may also be part of the Startup state (see Figure 11.1). Figure 11.23: Scenario: Report Supervision Failure Figure 11.23 illustrates the default scenario for Report Supervision Failure . As a precondition, State Management needs to call the method Offer() in order to register for notifications. Whenever Platform Health Management detects a supervision failure it notifies State Management by invoking the callback method RecoveryHandler() . If the call to State Management does not return within the timeout configured in the Man- ifest , Platform Health Management needs to call the method FireWatchdo- gReaction() to perform a restart of the Machine . During its shutdown State Management needs to call the method StopOffer() to disable further invocations of RecoveryHandler() . 11.5.1.3 Recover from Critical Supervision Failure 11.5.1.3.1 Scenario: Recover from Critical Supervision Failure in Execution Management

Please note the API defines the execution context of the termination handler to be a background thread which is maintained by the ara::exec::ExecutionClient . It is not executed in a signal handler context, therefore usage of POSIX and ara APIs is not restricted (potential restrictions in the contract of ara APIs still apply). During the Terminating state, the Process is expected to save persistent data and free all internally used resources. The Process indicates completion of the Termi- nating state by termination with exit status 0 ( EXIT_SUCCESS ). Execution Management as the parent Process can detect termination of the child Process and take the appropriate platform-specific actions such as processing exe- cution dependencies that rely on the Terminated state and thus ensure that there is no overlap between these Processes when both are running. 7.4 State Management 7.4.1 Overview State Management functional cluster defines the operational state of an AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform , while Execution Management performs the transitions be- tween different states. The Execution Manifest allows to define in which states the Modelled Pro- cesses have to run (see [3]). As mentioned before, a Modelled Process is an instance of an Executable , which is part of an Adaptive Application . State Management mechanisms grant full control over the set of applications to be executed and ensures that Processes are only executed (and hence resources allocated) when actually needed. Four different states are relevant for Execution Management : Execution State – An Execution States characterizes the internal lifecycle of each started Process , see Section 7.3.1 Process State – Process States are managed by an Execution Management internal state machine. For details see Section 7.3.2. Machine Sta…

The specification expects that State Management will be configured to run in ev- ery Machine State (this includes Startup , Shutdown and Restart ) [SWS_SM_ CONSTR_00001] [12]. Above expectation is needed in order to ensure that there is always a software entity that can introduce changes in the current state of the Ma- chine . If (for example) system integrator doesn’t configure State Management to be started in Startup Machine State , then Machine will never be able transit to any other state and will be stuck forever in it. This also applies to any other Machine State that doesn’t have State Management configured. The possibility that the Machine State transition to the Startup state is never reached shall be taken into account. In this case the State Management can inter- rupt the Startup state transition and request e.g. a recovery state using the ara:: exec::StateClient::SetState interface. Please note it is system integrator’s responsibility to carefully consider when system shutdown / restart should be requested because all Processes which are still running will not be terminated by Execution Management , which means that they will not be able to persist their data. As mentioned in Section 7.4.2.1, AUTOSAR assumes that State Management will be configured to run in Shutdown and Restart. State transition is not a trivial system change and it can fail for a number of reasons - in which case State Management should remain alive to report errors and wait for further instructions. Please note that the purpose of entering the Shutdown or Restart state is to shutdown or restart the Machine (this includes State Management ) in a clean manner. Conversely, the opposite procedure is expected during OS wake-up, with Adaptive Applications returning to their normal operational mode. In the StateMachine approach, the Controller is responsible for orchestrating state changes at the Machine level. To maintain consistent Suspend-to-RAM co- ordination and avoid conflicting or redundant requests, the StateMachine approach integrates the ara::sm::s2r::S2RHub functionality internally. Therefore, external applications such as the SMControlApplication are not allowed to access the ara::sm::s2r::S2RHub API when the StateMachine approach is used. This en- sures centralized control and prevents race conditions or state inconsistencies during suspend and wake-up transitions. Figure 7.40: Example for leaving Suspend-To-RAM 7.7.15.1 Autonomous wake-up from suspend state State Management is capable of reacting to wake-up triggers originating from mul- tiple sources. While the SMControlApplication may explicitly request a transition out of Suspend-to-RAM mode, State Management can also initiate a wake-up au- tonomously in response to system-level or an update session request. Specifically, if the operating system signals a wake-up via the apext::sm::Wake- UpHandler interface (if implemented), or if the Update and Configuration Management issues a RequestUpdateSession call while the Controller is in a suspend-related state, State Management will initiate a wake-up sequence.

In these cases, State Management performs the transition by moving the Con- troller from its current suspend-related StateMachine State to a designated wake-up StateMachine State . This autonomous behavior ensures that the Ma- chine can resume operation without requiring explicit coordination from the SMCon- trolApplication . To enable this autonomous transition, a dedicated wake-up StateMachine State has to be modeled and identifiable by State Management .
